subject: hotdog
title: Per-session CSPRNG aliasing of every protected wire marker: tool-call/thinking/summary tags, WireFormat-owned names, and model control tokens are rewritten to random m_<16-char> aliases before the model ever sees them, so untrusted text cannot forge a tool call or harness message even when it guesses the real tag name
evidence: src/core/marker-mangler.ts:16-46 (protected list, unbiased alias generation), src/core/llm-client/serialize.ts:61-98 (escape at wire incl. tool-call name/args), :110-112 (provenance decides trust: only system/harness exempt)
one_why: Injection defense structural rather than screening: the model never observes the real marker bytes, so a poisoned file quoting  or <tool_call> matches nothing; aliases are unescaped once on assembled stream output so deltas can't fossilize them (src/core/agent.ts:744-756); tests include alias-fossil and mangler-union suites.

subject: hotdog
title: Two-arm spoof defense: the mangler protects the model's eyes, spoof.ts protects the human's - bidi overrides/isolates, zero-widths, C0/C1, BOM become visible counted [U+XXXX] tokens at every human render boundary (approval prompts, tool display, webui), never at storage
evidence: src/utils/spoof.ts:1-20 (invariant), :37-40 (codepoint set), :56-67; choke points src/extensions/user-gate/index.ts:108, src/extensions/ui-interactive-cli/index.ts, src/extensions/webui/ui/utils.ts, src/utils/cli/cli.ts; tests tests/utils/spoof.test.ts, tests/extensions/user-gate.test.ts:87
one_why: The git-di<U+202E>ff class makes an approval prompt read differently from what runs; no other corpus subject neutralizes terminal control at display while keeping original bytes in the audit log; counting (not stripping) makes presence itself the alert.

subject: hotdog
title: Machine-wide provider-concurrency as a filesystem counting semaphore: atomic exclusive-create slots, rename-onto reclaim with read-back, mtime heartbeat leases provable from any host, WeakRef missed-release watchdog, and a capped phantom lane so unplaced traffic cannot bypass caps
evidence: src/core/session/lane-ledger.ts:1-60 (protocol incl. argued residual race), src/core/session/model-resolver.ts:56-80 (bare-name lane conservatism), src/core/session/turn-lanes.ts:1-30 (top-level turns hold the same slots, incl. mid-turn question holds), tests/core/lane-ledger.test.ts, lane-unplaced-capacity.test.ts
one_why: Local-first reality: an interactive session, a CLI workflow, and any other hotdog process hit the same llama.cpp endpoint; no other subject bounds subagent concurrency at machine scope with crash-reclaimable leases; deliberate fail-open on ledger FS errors prevents deadlock-by-state-dir.

subject: hotdog
title: Workflow runs journal state transitions to append-only run.jsonl, claim the run dir with a pid+host+heartbeat owner file (live-owner refusal, stale reclaim), and resume by reconciling completed claims against the filesystem (size+mtime freshness), reusing only what verifies
evidence: src/extensions/workflows/engine.ts:6-14 (design), :270-311 (claim + all-exit-path release), :1177+ (#resume workflow-name guard), tests/extensions/workflows-engine.test.ts:1095-1177 (reconcile validates/flags, resume reuses valid claims, refuses wrong workflow)
one_why: Crash recovery without a daemon: a killed run re-admits only unverified nodes, and double-driving is refused by liveness-checked ownership; this is the orchestrator this very field study runs on (t3-giant-review) - dogfooded durability at the same bar as codex journals.

subject: hotdog
title: Node acceptance is machine-checked: declared output files must exist and be fresh for the run, plus a <node>.verdict file whose first line is pass|fail|reject; an optional judge node re-gates with critique spliced verbatim into the producer's warm retry
evidence: src/extensions/workflows/engine.ts:662-700 (#evaluateGate freshness+verdict), :706-830 (#runJudge per-producer-attempt budget, deadlock-analyzed deps :540-560), :186-196 (spliced model-authored critique rides untrusted parts), tests workflows-engine.test.ts:325-346,805-1015
one_why: Converges with the validated-finish-gate cluster but adds the file-freshness claim (stale outputs from a prior run fail) and judge-verdict routing (reject vs fail selects retryOn buckets); a poisoned run-dir file cannot impersonate harness framing because splices are provenance-tagged.

subject: hotdog
title: Scheduler optimizes KV-cache warmth: spawn candidates are ordered by a cached llama-swap /running peek (loaded models beat all), gate-failed retries run as warm follow-up turns on the same parked session, and lane slots are held across mid-turn question waits so a swap cannot thrash the cache the user returns to
evidence: src/core/session/model-resolver.ts:11 ('cache warmth beats all'), :236 (warmSortCandidates), :426-455 (/running peeker, failures degrade), src/extensions/workflows/engine.ts:449-470 (warm retry comment 'KV cache stays warm'), src/core/session/turn-lanes.ts:12-15
one_why: pi warms caches; nobody else schedules a multi-model fleet around cache residency - on local hardware a cache miss is a minutes-scale stall, and CONTEXT.md:38 names cache invalidation 'can mean 20s vs 5m' as the critical perf concern the placement layer exists to serve.

subject: hotdog
title: Bash triage is a bail-based hand tokenizer, not a deny-list: tracks quoting at character level, segments on operators, follows cd, and BAILS to ask/deny on expansions, substitutions, globs, heredocs, eval/env/xargs, inline-code flags, find -exec - 'when it is unsure it asks'
evidence: src/utils/approvals/bash.ts:1-10 (scope statement incl. 'not a security boundary'), :52-146 (tokenizer bail rules), :210-229 (bail sets), src/extensions/user-gate/extension.json (default-deny: 'unverifiable is not allowed'), tests/utils/approvals/
one_why: Converges with the ferrum/kimi grammar-policy cluster without a parser dependency; the key soundness move is that every un-analyzable construct escalates rather than matches, and under default=deny a bail denies outright - the opposite polarity of the regex-denylist family.

subject: hotdog
title: Approvals are off by default: stock hotdog mediates no tool call - userGate.enabled=false means bash runs unconfirmed - and the always-on Workspace containment covers only file tools, so a single echo > ~/.ssh/x bypasses every default guard
evidence: src/extensions/user-gate/extension.json:10-14 (enabled default false), src/utils/approvals/bash.ts:9 ('Nothing below it enforces any boundaries'), src/utils/workspace.ts:285-355 (containment scope: file tools via resolveSafe only), src/core/tool-executor.ts:155-163 (gate pipeline exists but registers nothing when disabled)
one_why: This is why safety scores 5 and not the 6 of pi/cline/crush: their approval binds by default; hotdog's machinery is the best-tested fail-closed gate in the corpus (tests/extensions/user-gate.test.ts:245-388) and the honesty is exemplary, but real machinery + off-by-default is below the tested-approval rung, per the nanocoder precedent minus the deception.

subject: hotdog
title: Context-overflow rescue is LLM-free and self-guarding: on a provider overflow, trim drops the minimum that the same local estimate says fits; when the estimate itself lost the race, the blunt drop fires only if canCompact passes - so a misclassified overflow cannot silently eat a young session's history - then the single core retry ships the mutated params
evidence: src/extensions/compaction/index.ts:376-430 (PROVIDER_ERROR handler + canCompact gate comment), :400-410 (params.messages mutation), src/core/llm-client/retry.ts (isContextOverflowError)
one_why: The ladder deliberately avoids a summarize pass on a backend that just rejected a conversation-sized request; rung selection (trim vs drop) is decided by the very estimator that failed, with an explicit second-guess rule - converges with overflow-degradation-ladder with a novel misclassification guard.

subject: hotdog
title: Compaction trigger estimates the outgoing request at the session's wire size: tool-result parts are measured through the resolved WireFormat renderer, not at rest, so the projection approximates what the model actually receives including wrappers and mangling
evidence: src/extensions/compaction/utils.ts:63-70 (shouldCompact), :91-94 (estimatorFor renders parts via wire format), src/extensions/compaction/index.ts:357-362 (CONTEXT-hook trigger)
one_why: Same family as the x10 usage-measured cluster; the wire-size twist matters most on local backends where wrapper verbosity differs per format, and chars/4 stays honestly a heuristic with a documented misclassification guard in the overflow rung.

subject: hotdog
title: Tool-call/result pairing integrity is enforced at every truncation seam: finish_reason=length refuses to execute any call (args may be silently truncated) and synthesizes re-issue results for all of them; stopLoop mid-batch answers every stranded call; compaction boundaries back up over tool results so a kept window never starts orphaned
evidence: src/core/agent.ts:43-56,641-666 (length-stop + per-iteration cap), src/core/tool-executor.ts:93-106 (stopLoop skip-answers), src/extensions/compaction/utils.ts:42-58 + index.ts:174-183 (orphan safety net aborts compaction)
one_why: Strict OpenAI-compatible backends 400 a request containing an unanswered tool_call, so one truncation wedges the whole session; treating pairing as an invariant at every cut (including refusing unsafe execution rather than running truncated args) is the discipline most subjects rediscover via bricked histories.

subject: hotdog
title: tool-call-repair recovers local-model output: leaked Hermes/antml/chatML call markup in content or reasoning is grammar-parsed into real tool calls mid-loop, and a corrupt stored tool call (interrupt-truncated args that 400 every subsequent request) is dropped from history with one retry - unbricking the session
evidence: src/extensions/tool-call-repair/index.ts:1-14, grammar.ts:37-66 (Hermes/antml tag synonyms), src/core/agent.ts:329-339 (PROVIDER_ERROR one-retry repair seam)
one_why: Local backends leak template markup constantly; only the agent loop's own response is scanned (model-origin, not injection-origin), and the bricked-history path fixes the classic 'interrupted a hung call, session now permanently 400s' failure no cloud-first subject handles.

subject: hotdog
title: Zero runtime dependencies by construction with a written supply-chain posture: no install step, no build, no lifecycle hooks, bun.lock pins only @types/bun; the Bun runtime itself is named as the remaining trust boundary
one_why: Strongest supply-chain posture in the corpus (stronger than any anchor); minor nuance: docs/supply-chain.md:3 says 'no published artifact' while package.json:26 carries publishConfig.provenance for an npm publish path - one of three minor doc drifts, not a capability gap.

subject: hotdog
title: Loop breaker over canonicalized call signatures: JSON args re-serialized with sorted keys so cosmetic variants share a hash, detecting consecutive repeats and strict ping-pong, escalating nudge -> stronger nudge -> stop at t/2t/3t with per-episode state reset when the tail stops looping
one_why: Converges with crush's breaker (only anchor with one) and joins it in the corpus; the argument-canonicalization and level-ladder (intervene early and weakly before stopping) are the refinements worth counting toward convergence.

subject: hotdog
title: Loop driven in-process by programmable stream-event mocks plus an independent-oracle conformance tier: OpenAI wire-shape fixtures vendored from the official openai-openapi repo with declared derivation provenance ('never from hotdog output'), alongside MCP/SSE/retry-after conformance and golden-request suites
one_why: The oracle-independence declaration is the differentiator vs the x33 faux-provider cluster: protocol assertions are checked against captured third-party fixtures rather than regenerated from the implementation's own output; still in-process only - no subprocess/PTY e2e of the real CLI, which keeps verification at 7.
